fullDescription:
The classic Ha Long day trip from Hanoi, covering the three stops that define a first visit.

Twelve hours sounds long until you account for the road: Hanoi to Ha Long is around two and a half hours each way, so five of those twelve are spent getting there and back. The meeting point is the Hanoi Opera House, which is central and easy to find at dawn.

Sung Sot, the Surprise Cave, is the largest in the bay. It opens through a climb from the jetty into two enormous lit chambers, and the second one is big enough that the scale takes a moment to land. The name comes from the French, who found it in the 1900s and called it the Grotte des Surprises.

Luon Cave is the opposite: a low tunnel through the base of a karst that small boats pass through, opening into a lagoon enclosed by cliffs on every side. You go through in a bamboo boat or kayak rather than the cruise boat, because the ceiling is barely above head height at high tide.

Ti Top Island has both a beach and a staircase. The climb is around 400 steps to a viewpoint where the karsts spread out to the horizon in every direction, and it is the photograph most people come home with. The island is named after a Soviet cosmonaut who visited with Ho Chi Minh in 1962.

We book with Thao Nguyen Travel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers bus pickup and drop-off at the Hanoi Opera House, bottled water and an English-speaking guide throughout.

Twelve hours. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Sung Sot: two vast chambers, named by the French in the 1900s
Luon Cave by bamboo boat, under a ceiling barely head-high
Ti Top Island and its 400-step horizon view
Named after a Soviet cosmonaut who came with Ho Chi Minh
Pickup at the Hanoi Opera House, five hours of the day on the road

fullDescription:
One night on the water covering both Ha Long and Lan Ha, in a deluxe en-suite cabin.

The two bays matter as a pair. Ha Long proper is the famous one and carries most of the fleet; Lan Ha sits immediately south off Cat Ba, the same drowned karst landscape with around 300 islands and a fraction of the boats. A route that takes in both shows you the postcard and the quiet version in the same trip, and only an overnight can reach Lan Ha at all.

The case for sleeping on board is what happens either side of the night. From late afternoon the day boats head back to port and the bay empties out; by the time you are eating dinner there are a handful of lights on the water instead of a hundred. Morning is the same in reverse, and the hours before the fleet returns are the quietest Ha Long ever gets.

The cabin is fully furnished and en-suite rather than a bunk with a shared bathroom, with a welcome drink, cold handkerchief, fruit basket and bottled water waiting in it.

One practical detail true of every boat in this bay: air conditioning runs to a schedule, typically overnight rather than continuously, so days on deck are warm. That is fleet-wide and not specific to this cruise.

We book with La Pandora Cruises directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the deluxe en-suite cabin and the welcome drink, cold handkerchief, fruit basket and mineral water in each cabin.

Two days, one night. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Both bays: famous Ha Long and quiet Lan Ha
Lan Ha is only reachable on an overnight, not a day trip
The fleet leaves at dusk and returns after dawn
Deluxe en-suite cabin, not a bunk with a shared bathroom
Boat air conditioning runs overnight, so decks are warm by day

fullDescription:
A night on the bay aboard a junk, with entrance fees and the Hanoi transfer available as one package.

The junk is the traditional Vietnamese sailing hull with the distinctive battened sails, and the modern cruise versions keep the silhouette while running on engines. It is the shape in every photograph of this bay, and being on one rather than looking at one is most of the appeal.

What an overnight buys you is the bay without the fleet. Day boats turn for port in the late afternoon, and from then until the next morning the water holds a handful of lights instead of a hundred. Dinner and sunrise both happen in that window.

Kayaking or a bamboo boat is included, which is how you get into the places the cruise boat cannot: Luon Cave is a low tunnel through the base of a karst into an enclosed lagoon, and the ceiling is barely above head height at high tide.

All entrance fees are covered, which on this bay is not a small line. That covers the bay entry fee and the separate charges at the caves and at Ti Top, so nothing is collected at the jetties.

Transport from Hanoi is available as an option rather than standard, so check whether yours includes it: the drive is around two and a half hours each way.

We book with Ruby Tour directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the two-day one-night cruise, an English-speaking guide, all entrance fees and kayaking or a bamboo boat, with Hanoi transport if your option includes it.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: A traditional junk hull, the shape in every photograph
Overnight, when the bay holds a handful of lights
Kayak or bamboo boat into Luon Cave's low tunnel
All entrance fees covered, including the caves and Ti Top
Check whether Hanoi transport is in your chosen option

fullDescription:
A deluxe ocean-view suite on a five-star cruise working both Ha Long and Lan Ha.

The suite is the product here. An ocean-view room on a cruise boat means you wake up looking at karsts rather than at a corridor, and on a trip where the best hours are dawn and dusk that is not a detail. In-room tea and coffee, bottled water and daily fresh fruit come with it, along with a welcome drink and cold towel on arrival.

The route covering both bays is the other half. Ha Long proper is where the fleet concentrates; Lan Ha, immediately south off Cat Ba, is the same drowned karst with around 300 islands and far fewer boats. Day trips from Hanoi cannot reach Lan Ha at all, so a multi-day cruise is the only way to see the quiet half.

The overnight itself is what people underrate. From late afternoon the day boats leave and the bay empties; dinner, night and sunrise all happen with the water almost to yourself. By the time the day fleet returns you have already had the best of it.

One detail that applies across this bay and not just this boat: air conditioning in cabins runs to a schedule, usually overnight rather than continuously, so the deck is warm during the day.

We book with An Lam Ha Long Tourism Services directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the deluxe ocean-view suite aboard the five-star Amanda Cruise, welcome drink, cold towel, in-room tea, coffee, bottled water and daily fresh fruit.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Deluxe ocean-view suite, so you wake facing the karsts
Covers Lan Ha, which day trips from Hanoi cannot reach
Dinner, night and sunrise with the bay almost empty
In-room tea, coffee, water and daily fresh fruit
Cabin air conditioning runs overnight, not all day

fullDescription:
Four days and two nights on the water, taking in the parts of this coast that day trips never reach.

Viet Hai village is the reason to give this trip four days. It sits in a valley on Cat Ba Island, ringed by karst and reachable only by boat and then a walk or cycle, and until recently had no road at all. It is a working farming village rather than a display, and getting there is the whole point: nothing on a Ha Long day cruise goes near it.

The Dark and Bright Cave is the other stop day trips skip. You go through in a bamboo boat: one tunnel in complete darkness, then out into a bright enclosed lagoon on the other side, which is where the name comes from.

Lan Ha Bay is the quieter bay south of Ha Long proper, around 300 islands off Cat Ba, where the big fleet does not go. Kayaking and swimming happen here rather than in the busy channels.

Ninh Binh closes the trip with the inland version of the same limestone: karst towers rising out of rice paddies and a river instead of the sea.

Two nights are spent on a cruise, one in Ninh Binh, and the cruise standard runs from 3-star to 5-star depending on the option selected.

We book with SST Travel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers Hanoi Old Quarter pickup and drop-off, two nights aboard a 3, 4 or 5-star cruise, one night in Ninh Binh, kayaking and swimming, Viet Hai village and the Dark and Bright Cave.

Four days. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Viet Hai village: boat-only, in a karst valley on Cat Ba
Dark and Bright Cave by bamboo boat, tunnel then lagoon
Lan Ha Bay, where the big fleet does not go
Two nights on the water and one in Ninh Binh
Karst at sea and then inland, in one trip

fullDescription:
Three days across both UNESCO karst landscapes, with the driving handled by limousine.

Ha Long and Ninh Binh are the same limestone doing two different things. In Ha Long the towers rise out of the sea; in Ninh Binh they rise out of rice paddies with a river running between them, which is why it gets called the inland bay. Seeing them a day apart is what makes the pair register as one landscape rather than two attractions.

Lan Ha is the part worth paying for. It lies immediately south of Ha Long proper, off Cat Ba, and holds around 300 islands of the same drowned karst with a fraction of the boats, because the large fleet stays in Ha Long. A day trip from Hanoi cannot get there; an overnight can.

The night on the water is where the bay is quietest. Day boats leave in the late afternoon and return after dawn, so dinner, the night and sunrise all happen with a handful of lights on the water instead of a hundred.

Ninh Binh is Tam Coc by rowing boat through three river caves, rowed by locals working the oars with their feet, and the climb at Mua Cave, several hundred stone steps to a dragon on the ridge.

Limousine transfer between Hanoi, Ha Long and Ninh Binh means reclining seats across several hundred kilometres rather than a coach bench.

We book with SST Travel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers Hanoi Old Quarter pickup and drop-off, limousine transfers throughout, and one night on a 3, 5 or 6-star luxury cruise depending on the option chosen.

Three days. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Both UNESCO karst landscapes: at sea and inland
Lan Ha Bay, unreachable on a day trip from Hanoi
A night on the water after the day fleet leaves
Tam Coc by rowing boat and the Mua Cave ridge climb
Limousine across all three legs, not a coach
